A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Indian caste system is not genetically determined, as the genetic heritage of the Indian tribes persists both in tribal and caste populations.
the Indian caste system has been a very effective social mechanism in maintaining genetic diversity, and this diversity is a reflection of a very ancient and complex history.

the genetic diversity of the earliest human settlers in India persists in both tribal and caste populations and that the Indian tribal and caste groups are not significantly different from each other in their genetic heritage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chenchus, Koyas, and Indian castes are all descended from the same Pleistocene settlers of southern and western Asia.
the Chenchu and Koya tribes are not isolated genetic isolates.
